draft.title: Physical activity, exercise and sport
card: Physical activity
any movement of the body that uses energy. It includes play, games, active transport, chores, exercise, recreation and sport.
Exercise
planned, structured activity done to improve or keep up fitness or health, such as a gym session or a training run.
Sport
activity with rules and a focus on skill and competition. It can be formal, such as a club netball match, or informal, such as a kick of the footy at the park.
Exercise and sport are both types of physical activity. Walking to school or mowing the lawn counts as physical activity, but it is not exercise or sport.
draft.remember: Physical activity is the big group. Exercise and sport are two types inside it.

a.q: Which of these is physical activity but is not exercise or sport?
opts: Cycling to school each morning
Playing in a club football match
Doing a planned gym program
Running laps at squad training
a.why: Cycling to school is movement that uses energy, but it is for travel, not for fitness training or competition. The gym program is planned to build fitness, so it is exercise, and the football match is sport.
a.clue: Which one is done to get somewhere, not to train or compete?

b.q: Priya mows her family's lawn every Saturday. It takes an hour and she gets out of breath. How is this best described?
opts: Physical activity, because it uses energy
Exercise, because it makes her puffed
Sport, because it takes effort and time
Not physical activity, because it is a chore
b.why: Mowing the lawn is body movement that uses energy, so it is physical activity. It is not planned to improve fitness, so it is not exercise, and it has no rules or competition, so it is not sport. Getting puffed does not turn a chore into exercise.
b.clue: Was the main aim to improve fitness, or to get a job done?

b.best: Physical activity, because it uses energy

problems.detail: The card gives 'a kick of the footy at the park' as informal sport, but it has just defined sport as activity with rules and a focus on competition. A casual kick has neither, so the example clashes with the definition. A social game with informal rules, such as backyard cricket, would fit better.
